name: Paletka
description:
Switch whole-desktop color themes (shell, apps, terminal, Text Editor, VS Code, wallpaper, icons) from Quick Settings, and create your own in a built-in editor. Ships Ubuntu, Solarized, Gruvbox, Nord and Dracula.

To theme apps, Paletka writes ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css, installs adw-gtk3 and generated GTK3 themes into ~/.local/share/themes, changes GNOME, Ptyxis, GNOME Terminal and Text Editor settings and the color theme keys of VS Code's settings.json, and restarts Files (waiting while it copies, moves, deletes or shows a dialog) and the desktop portal so they pick up the new colors. Everything is backed up first: choosing Ubuntu, turning Paletka off or uninstalling it restores your original look.

It stays enabled on the lock screen (unlock-dialog) so the shell keeps its colors there; the Theme tile is hidden while locked.
